newsitem.title: USA: Mark junk bonds to fund Pechiney, Schmalbach deal.
newsitem.headline: Mark junk bonds to fund Pechiney, Schmalbach deal.

text.p: The upcoming merger of the metal packaging units of Pechiney SA and Schmalbach-Lubeca AG will be financed in part by a rare Deutschemark-denominated junk bond offering in Europe and the United States, market sources said.
It will be only the third time junk bonds have been denominated in marks. The first two mark-denominated junk bond deals priced in recent weeks.
Schmalbach is a subsidiary of German industrial group VIAG AG.
Impress Metal Packaging, the company to be formed from the units, will issue up to 200 million marks of high-yield bonds via Salomon Brothers Inc in early May, the sources added.
Salomon Brothers declined to comment on the deal.
The 1.2 billion mark merger is being financed as a leveraged buyout, led by Doughty Hanson & Co, a British leveraged buyout (LBO), or venture fund.
Market sources said junk-bond financing for the deal will be supplemented with an 840 million mark bank credit facility syndicated by Union Bank of Switzerland, and 250 million marks in equity.

Following completion of the transaction, Impress will be 60 percent owned by Doughty Hanson, and 20 percent owned by each of Pechiney and Schmalbach. Impress will be incorporated in the Netherlands, sources said.
The Impress 144a Euronote offering will consist of 10-year senior subordinated notes, non-callable for five years, market sources said.
The European roadshow for the offering was expected to begin in late April, they added.

Doughty Hanson also led the recent leveraged buyout of Geberit International SA, which was financed by the first-ever mark denominated junk bond offering. Geberit's 150 million mark offering of 10-year notes, which priced on April 10, was underwritten by Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.
On Thursday, Exide Holdings Europe SA sold 175 million marks of seven-year 144a high-yield Euronotes via Morgan Stanley & Co.
